Thanks,

Thanks for the ping — read the logs. Quick summary from runtime side:

- Observed behavior: fallback path uses a smaller variant with different tokenization/temperature defaults; for very long contexts we also hit a different KV-cache path which can truncate context slightly. That combination can lead to shorter/less coherent outputs.
- Hotfix options (fastest first):
  1) Temporary routing override for deal HS-4321 to pin to the +8B variant (we can do per-account routing rules today; however it bypasses autoscaling and may be rate-limited under high load). Estimated turnaround: ~6 hours to test + rollout as a scoped rule.
  2) Quality-guard rule: add a validation that, during fallback, we verify expected token-length/entropy thresholds and if below threshold, re-queue to the larger variant (more invasive). ETA: 3-5 days engineering work.
  3) Short-term client-side suggestion: trim prefix to reduce context length or use on-the-fly chunking from the app — works but requires customer changes.

Questions for Sales/CS:
- Is NovaProd willing to accept temporary throughput limits if we pin them to the larger variant?
- Can they provide a reproducible prompt set (10-20 prompts) we can run as a regression test?

I'll start a scoped routing rule draft (option 1) if you authorize. Also filing SUP-7832 to track the follow-up engineering work on the fallback quality guard.

— Logan
Runtime Engineering Lead
